testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal and the S-cam turns, what does it do?

options.text: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Tightens the brake drum onto the axle.
Pushes the brake lining against the wheel.
Releases air from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal and the S-cam turns, it pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle down.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles use air brake systems. These systems use compressed air to operate the brakes.

questions.question: What makes up the emergency brake system?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three separate braking systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too often can release air faster than the compressor can replace it. If air pressure drops too low, the air brakes may stop working.

questions.question: Where are ABS malfunction lamps located on trucks and buses?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle by the passenger's door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lights on the instrument panel. Trailers have yellow ABS warning lights on the left side, either on the front or rear.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate allowed for a single vehicle with air brakes during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: You need to know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A single vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 3 psi of pressure in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: What should you do when leaving your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Lower the windows in the cab.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: What does the emergency brake system use?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system.
Only parts of the service brake system.
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems.
Only parts unique to the emergency brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems.
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three separate braking systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the air compressor breaks down, neither system will work properly.

questions.question: What color warning light does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) use when it is not working properly?
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) warning lights are usually yellow. Even if the ABS is not working properly, you will still have regular braking functions.

questions.question: Which braking system uses the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Shift into a lower gear, then use the brakes to help slow the vehicle.
Downshift continuously instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear, then use the brakes to help slow the vehicle.
questions.explanation: On a downgrade, use the engine's braking power as your main way to control speed. Shift down to a lower gear before you go down the hill. Use the brakes only when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What holds spring brakes in place while you are driving?
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while you drive. If air pressure drops low enough, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times
Push in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: The parking brake is controlled by a knob. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes. Push the knob in to release them.

questions.question: If only the tractor has Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what happens?

options.text: There is a lower risk of jackknifing.
There is a higher risk of jackknifing.
The brakes will not work as well without ABS.
The brakes will become more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a lower risk of jackknifing.
questions.explanation: If the tractor has ABS but the trailer does not, the risk of jackknifing is reduced. You should still be able to steer the vehicle. If only the trailer has ABS, the trailer is less likely to swing out to one side.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle must not lose more than 6 psi of air in one minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: How do you remove water and oil from an air storage tank?

options.text: Siphon the water and oil out of the tank.
Open a drain valve to remove the water and oil.
The water and oil are removed automatically when you use the brakes.
Use a sponge to soak up the water and oil.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open a drain valve to remove the water and oil.
questions.explanation: Use a drain valve to remove water and oil from air storage tanks. Water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Manually operated tanks must be drained every day.

questions.question: When does an air compressor governor stop pumping air?

options.text: When the air tanks reach 125 psi.
When the air tanks reach 100 psi.
When the air tanks reach 150 psi.
When the air tanks reach 80 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air tanks reach 125 psi.
questions.explanation: The governor stops the compressor from pumping air when the tanks reach 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park your vehicle.

questions.question: What is true about a dual air brake system?

options.text: Each system has its own separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
The systems share air tanks, but each has its own hoses and lines.
Both systems use the same lines and hoses.
One system is the main system, and the second system only works if the first one fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own separate air tanks, hoses, and lines.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share one brake control, but each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: What happens if you press and release the brake pedal too many times?

options.text: Air is released faster than the compressor can replace it.
More air is added to the braking system.
The brake pedal becomes more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air is released faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too many times causes air to leave the system faster than the compressor can put it back.

questions.question: How should you use your brakes when going down a steep hill?

options.text: Hold the brakes down the entire hill.
Apply the brakes for a few seconds, release them for a few seconds, and repeat this pattern down the hill.
Only use the brakes near the bottom of the hill.
Keep steady pressure on the brake pedal the whole way down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes for a few seconds, release them for a few seconds, and repeat this pattern down the hill.
questions.explanation: On steep hills, use the engine to help slow your vehicle. Apply brakes until you feel the vehicle slow down, then release them. When the vehicle reaches a safe speed again, repeat this process.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes located?

options.text: Only at the driver's side wheels.

questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are located at each wheel. The most common type is the S-cam drum brake.
